decision_rule.text: Apply in order, first trigger decides. V0 integrity FAIL on any certification arm -> NO RULING. V1 rate(AB12) < 25 -> NO RULING (driver not reproducing the known containment failure). A1 NOT CERTIFIED(AB4) -> ABANDON. A2 AB14b power < 90% -> ABANDON. A3 rate(AB1) > 8.0 -> ABANDON. A4 rate(AB6) > 8.0 -> ABANDON. A5 rate(AB15) > 8.0 -> ABANDON. Otherwise KEEP, GATED at m* = min clusters-per-cell over certified cluster-VCE arms, n* = min cluster count, cell* = min cell size over certified robust arms. AME sub-ruling: keep ame adversarial iff AB9 ame rej@.05 in [15,35] and chi2 <= 21.666, else WITHDRAW to RI/bootstrap/IM. ALT sub-ruling: keep altmethod iff CERTIFIED(AB11).

amendment_1.disclosure: Added AFTER partial results from the original 19 configs were seen (AB1-AB12 complete). This is an amendment, not part of the original preregistration, and is disclosed as such. Predictions for AB17-AB21 were nonetheless LOCKED before these five configs ran. All five are report-only diagnostics; they cannot enter the certified set and cannot change the original decision rule's triggers.
amendment_1.purpose: The original grid measured altmethod_adversarial only where standard adversarial PASSES (AB11), so it could not answer whether one method is salvageable when the other is not. These five are CRN-paired altmethod twins of every regime where standard adversarial FAILED: small cells (AB3), containment (AB12), violated VCE (AB7b), few clusters (AB5), and robust+AR(1) inertness (AB8).
amendment_1.rule: ALT-INDEPENDENT: altmethod_adversarial is worth keeping independently of adversarial iff it CERTIFIES (PASS band + chi2 <= 21.666) in at least one regime where its paired standard twin FAILED. If it merely reduces the failure magnitude without certifying anywhere new, the two stand or fall together and altmethod is at most a documented mild improvement. Conversely if CERTIFIED(AB11) and NOT CERTIFIED(AB1), altmethod is promoted to the documented default.

amendment_2.disclosure: Added after the AB campaign reported. Report-only; cannot enter the certified set or move any trigger. Prediction LOCKED before the config ran.
amendment_2.purpose: Third point on the ame cell-size ladder: 31.55% at U=6 (A4, robust), 9.92% at U=20 (AB9, robust), and now U=50. Tests whether the leverage mechanism (bias ~ within-cell parameters / cell size) continues to nominal or hits a floor from another channel.
amendment_2.locked_reasoning: Excess over nominal fell 26.5pp -> 4.9pp for a 3.3x cell-size increase. A further 2.5x predicts excess ~1.5pp, i.e. ~6.5%. The M=504 PASS band is [2.98,6.94]%, so the prediction sits at the certification edge: this config can genuinely go either way, which is what makes it worth running.

amendment_3.disclosure: Report-only; predictions LOCKED before running. Cannot enter the certified set or move an original trigger.
amendment_3.purpose: Binary results at 50 observations per cell across VCEs, including 50 clusters per cell. AB25 is the decisive one: it holds cell size at 50 while dropping to 2 clusters per cell, which separates the clusters-per-cell account (predicting failure regardless of cell size) from any account in which large cells are themselves protective. AB26 and AB28 extend the containment and common-shock ladders to large cells, where both are predicted to get WORSE, not better.
amendment_3.shared_seed_note: All six share base 9000001, so they are CRN-paired to each other (identical datasets across VCEs).

amendment_4.purpose: Completes the clustered continuous ladder. Measured so far: unit clustering at 6 units/cell = 48.41% (vs robust 31.55% on identical geometry), and robust at 20/50 units = 9.92%/5.95%. The clustered arm at 20 and 50 units was never run, so 'fine clustering harms the ame' rests on a single small-cell observation.
amendment_4.locked_reasoning: Two distinct channels damage the ame covariance and BOTH should improve with cell size: (1) leverage deflation of the within-cell dose slopes, which robust showed dies out by 50 units; (2) noisy cross-horizon off-diagonals that clustering estimates where robust sets them near zero - these are estimated from the cluster count, which grows with U. So I predict the clustered arm largely recovers by 50 units (6.5%) rather than staying at 48%, which would mean the harm from clustering is a SMALL-CELL phenomenon, not a property of clustering as such.
